title: pkix-path: ~45 survivors left, led by the name-constraint intersection
description:
## Why

pkix-path's sweep found 100 survivors; roughly 45 remain after five rounds
of fixes. Grouped by what they are about.

## Clusters

**Name-constraint intersection in chain_walk.** The `subtree_within` calls
and `already_in_result`. This is RFC 5280 §6.1.4 (g) permitted/excluded
subtree intersection -- the machinery that makes a constraint on an
intermediate bind everything below it. Highest value of what is left:
a wrong intersection is a trust-scope defect, which is the class the
§4.2.1.10 and SMTP-DANE findings earlier in this sweep belonged to.

**§6.1.1 path length.** `>` to `>=` on the max-path-length comparison, and
the `max_chain_certs` arithmetic. Boundary cases, the same shape as the CRL
and OCSP freshness windows closed in pkix-revocation: inclusive at the
documented end, and nothing asserts which end.

**policy_graph (3).** RFC 5280 §6.1.3/§6.1.4 policy mapping and the
valid-policy tree.

**sha1_digest (3).** Verify-only, opt-in per the project stance. Pinning it
needs a known-answer vector, which is a two-line test against the RFC 3174
sample.

**serde_der.rs (11).** The DER serde shims. Same class as
pkix-revocation's `crl_reason_serde`, where a round-trip over every variant
with hand-written wire values killed all eleven -- that is the template.

**check_max_validity.** One comparison.

**NormalizedIter / DirStringBytes (5).** RFC 4518 string prep internals
feeding `names_match`. Behavioural, and `names_match` is security-relevant;
these want direct unit tests on the iterator rather than tests through DN
comparison.

**Public helpers with no in-crate caller.** `cert_is_ca`,
`tbs_certificate_der`. A crate-scoped sweep cannot reach them by
construction; consumers may cover them, and that needs checking per case
rather than assuming either way. `pkix-identity`'s
`dns_name_matches_pattern` was the same shape and did turn out to be
entirely untested.

## Method

Re-run to regenerate the list:

    cargo mutants -p pkix-path --all-features -j 4 --timeout-multiplier 4

Six mutants timed out on the first run; `--timeout-multiplier 4` is what
keeps a slow-but-correct test from being read as a hang.

## Found by

The pkix-path mutation sweep, 2026-11-27: 552 mutants, 100 missed.
notes:
## The full sweep, and why it mattered

541 mutants, 472 caught, 8 missed, 56 unviable, 5 timeouts, 31 minutes
(-j 3, -E 'tests_|_tests::').

I had closed 18 survivors by hand and reported the crate down to one.
The sweep found eight: the one equivalent mutant I expected, and seven
real ones my hand-verification had missed or misjudged. All seven are now
closed -- e4cbe537, 20fd63e6, 28441573 -- each mutation hand-verified.

### The two I had misjudged

check_san_name_form's unevaluable-name-form guard, which I recorded this
morning as subsumed by check_name_constraints' generic SAN loop. True,
and true only because every fixture put the form in a PERMITTED subtree,
where the refusal is overdetermined: a name the matchers cannot decide
matches no subtree, and a constrained type matching nothing is a
violation, so the generic check refuses it whether or not the guard ran.
An EXCLUDED subtree inverts it -- matching nothing means matching no
exclusion, so the certificate passes and the guard is the only thing
refusing it. Same inversion for check_mailbox_against_rfc822's ASCII
requirement. Both fail open in the direction that widens a CA's trust
scope past what it published.

### The two I had never seen

chain_walk's `if i == 0` on required_leaf_policy_oids and
required_leaf_subject_dn_attrs. Mutated to `i != 0` each requirement
applies to every certificate except the leaf, so a leaf failing it is
accepted whenever an intermediate satisfies it. Invisible because the
only chain testing them is PKITS AllCertificatesSamePoliciesTest10 --
every certificate asserts the same policies, so no verdict it produces
can distinguish the leaf from the rest of the path.

### The policy_graph cluster

apply_policy_mappings' has_any, intersect_user_policy_set's node lookup,
and prune_above_deepest. All three shape the valid_policy_graph rather
than the verdict, and the §6.1.5 walk counts nodes and parents, so a
wrong shape answers the wrong question without failing. Tested against
the graph directly. Reaching the second took three attempts: the policy
must arrive below depth 1 through a mapping, its ancestor must stay in
the user set, and the leaf step needs may_expand_any_policy. That
arrangement is in the test's rustdoc.

### What remains

One missed mutant: NcTypeMask::RFC822's `1 << 0`, where `1 >> 0` is also
1. Equivalent, unkillable, noted in nc_type_mask_tests.

Five timeouts: the DirStringBytes and NormalizedIter next/position
mutants, which produce iterators that never return None. names_match
consumes them to exhaustion, so the suite detects them by not finishing;
a timeout is the only verdict available. Two bounded direct tests fail
in seconds when run alone. The sixth timeout is gone -- Peekable::next_if_eq
removed that comparison from the mutation space, confirmed with --list.

Both lessons generalised into AGENTS.md (995d33e1).
